correctness.rationale: The nontrivial fixed points solve a polynomial of degree exactly \(M\). Attracting roots require an inward positive-to-negative sign crossing and must be separated by other roots, so \(2k-1\le M\). For arbitrary ordered roots of sum at most one half, the exact quotient \(Q(y)=[1-R(y)/R(1)]/(1-y)\) has coefficients \(q_j=C^{-1}\sum_{s=0}^{M-j-1}(-1)^s e_s>0\), since \(\sum_{s=1}^M e_s\le\sum_{s=1}^M2^{-s}<1\). The identity \(f(y)=-yR(y)/C\) gives \(M\) simple positive fixed points and alternating attracting derivative signs, attaining \(\lceil M/2\rceil\) for every \(M\). The six-body rational witness is exact. Standard-library exact-rational replay passed \(M=1,\ldots,18\); finite tests were not used as proof of the universal statement.

value.rationale: The 2023 primary paper explicitly raises the arbitrary-endemic-level direction and the 2025 follow-up leaves higher-order global classification open. This result computes a sharp stable-endemic multiplicity ceiling, gives a strict-positive transmissibility inverse design rather than an arbitrary sign-unconstrained polynomial, establishes minimal \(2k\)-body interactions for \(k\) coexisting endemic attractors, and provides an exact six-body tristability witness on the fully homogeneous structure, open under rate perturbation. The finite example is motivated by the structural cutoff, not an arbitrary isolated computation.
